curriculum.lesson_evidence: Fridge storage is a drip-control system. Ready-to-eat food, such as leftovers in a closed container, fruit and dairy, sits above raw meat. Raw meat and chicken go on the bottom shelf in a covered tray so juice cannot fall onto food that will not be cooked. The fridge should be cold enough that food is at or below 5°C. Overpacking blocks airflow, so a very full fridge may have warm spots.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Draw or describe a four-shelf fridge holding raw sausages, a cream cake, apples and an open tin of leftover beans. Where does each go, and what must be covered?

FEEDBACK
Sausages on the bottom in a covered container. Cake and apples above them. Beans moved into a closed container, not stored in the open tin, and placed with ready-to-eat food above the sausages.

WATCH FOR
Putting raw chicken on the top shelf “so you remember it”. Memory is not a drip control.

Sausages on the bottom in a covered container. Cake and apples above them. Beans moved into a closed container, not stored in the open tin, and placed with ready-to-eat food above the sausages.
